Note that `_selectedIds` contains `selectedIds` but not `input.selectedIds`, so the expected_output's `input._selectedIds` does not trip the new forbidden token. The dev's script reports 0 forbidden hits across the file. The prompt is unchanged; the PR body says earlier records are set apart on regrade.

**Changeset, sentence by sentence:** "a bulk action is wired by the list view (`bulkActions`, or a `bulkActionDefs` entry with `execution: 'aggregate'`) and its body reads `input._selectedIds`, not `input.selectedIds`; the new-tab example's `target` uses `${ctx.recordId}` on `record_header`." The `_selectedIds` clause holds for the aggregate wiring only. The `bulkActions` wiring runs per row with `recordId`, as the rule bullet says, so the changeset compresses two wirings into one clause. See N1.

**Customer-seat value read:** an agent following the old row wrote a body that read an empty selection or hit the near-miss refusal. Now it learns both wirings and the exact key, for +5 lines within the ratchet (3709/3711).

**Non-blocking notes:**

- N2. The `list_toolbar` row "its body never gets the selection" is exact for the id array. With exactly one ticked row the button does get that row as `recordId`. The rule bullet covers the wirings, so this is wording only.

**Landing:** Tier H (`skills/**`). The seat's contract read is next.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Check-runs on the head.** 28 `success`, 16 `skipped`, none red or pending. `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Check Changeset` and `Governed Surface Queue Guard` are green. Inside `Type Check · source gates`, the steps "Published skills token ratchet (#10473) + its self-test" and "Check generated skill references are in sync with the spec" read `success`.
- **Surface.** Three files, 18 added, 13 deleted: one rule file and one eval fixture under `skills/**`, and one changeset. No schema, no runtime, no ratchet row, no generator. No accept set and no public surface moves.
- **What a body receives, read in the code and not from the PR body.**
  - Toolbar button. `resolveServerActionRecordId` in `ui/packages/core/src/actions/serverActionHandler.ts`: with no `_selectedIds` in the bag, one ticked row becomes `recordId`, several ticked rows are refused before the request, and none sends no record. No id array is sent under any key, so the old row named a key no path delivers. The new row is right about the id array; see N1.
  - Per-row wiring. `resolveBulkActions.ts` promotes a `bulkActions` name to a def carrying the action, and `runBulkActionRecord` in `ObjectGrid.tsx` dispatches once per row with that row stashed, which resolves to `recordId`. The bullet's first clause is right.
  - Aggregate wiring. `wantsAggregateResolve` in `resolveBulkActions.ts` asks for exactly `operation: 'custom'`, `execution: 'aggregate'` and a name, which is the entry the bullet spells. `runBulkActionAggregate` dispatches once and adds `_selectedIds` to the collected params; `packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts` hands the bag on as `params`; `buildActionSandboxContext` in `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/body-runner.ts` sets a body's `input` to it. `input._selectedIds` is the key. Right.
  - The example's param still reaches its dialog. `resolvePromotedBulkParams` resolves the named action's own `params` when the def authors none, so `campaign_id` is asked once for the selection.
  - The example's return. `useBulkExecutor.ts` reads a value with neither list as covering the whole selection, so a body that returns nothing reports every row. Dropping the `return` line changes no outcome.
  - The example's `execution: 'aggregate'`. It is `ActionSchema`'s own key (`packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts`), the declaration `action-dispatch-contract-mismatch` is measured against, and it names the side this body is written for.
  - Placement without `locations`. `packages/lint/src/validate-action-locations.ts` counts a `bulkActionDefs` name as a placement. Right; see N2.
- **The refusal clause is wider than the enforcement.** See S2.
- **New-tab example.** `interpolateTarget` in `ui/packages/core/src/actions/ActionRunner.ts` builds its scopes from `param` and `ctx` only, and `buildInterpolationContext` sets `ctx.recordId` from the record the header binds. `action.zod.ts` lists the same two families and names `ctx.recordId`. The example now uses a hole the runner fills, on a location that has a record. It meets the fold row's Done-when.
- **Eval case 3.** The file parses. Every `must_contain` token of the case is in its own `expected_output`, and neither forbidden token is: `input._selectedIds` does not contain `input.selectedIds`. Case 23 of the same file already teaches the aggregate key and agrees with the new text. See N4.
- **No other teaching is left contradicting it.** `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` and `content/docs/ui/views.mdx` already teach both wirings, `params._selectedIds` and the action-side `execution` key, in the same words the bullet now uses. No other file under `skills/**` or `ui/skills/**` names the selection key or places a bulk action. One example app outside the diff still carries the old shape; see ③.

### ② Semver level

`'@objectstack/skills': patch` is right: the package ships the `skills/**` tree, and this changes sentences, two examples and one eval case in it. `Clause-②: no` is right: nothing widens or narrows an accept set or the public surface, and no arm is owed. `Metadata-protocol: none` is right: nothing a metadata author can write changes, and `none` takes `patch`. Both lines are bare and line-initial in the PR body and in the changeset body. No `Rule-change:` line is owed, because no path is under `.claude/**`.

No must-fix. Two findings owe a delta review of their fix: S1 here and S2 under ④.

**S1 (should-fix) — the changeset sentence gives `input._selectedIds` to both wirings.** It reads: "a bulk action is wired by the list view (`bulkActions`, or a `bulkActionDefs` entry with `execution: 'aggregate'`) and its body reads `input._selectedIds`". Under `bulkActions` the body gets one `recordId` per call and no `_selectedIds`. The rule file says so correctly; the changeset does not. This sentence becomes the package changelog, which is what an upgrading author greps for the old key. An app built on the old teaching that follows it (name the action in `bulkActions`, rename the key) gets a body that reads nothing on every call and still reports success, the same outcome this PR removes, and no lint catches it while the action declares no `execution`. Say that the ids arrive only through the aggregate entry and that `bulkActions` runs per row with `recordId`. This is L1's note N1, graded here. The changeset is a prose face, so this fix alone does not move a reviewed file.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **The card's Done-when is met, apart from S2.** The text and the example name the key the dispatch code delivers, and eval case 3 pins it. The fold row is fixed in the same file. `Fixes` is the right keyword; the fold row's checkbox is the seat's to tick.

Fixing the fold row in place is inside the card, since `Fixes` would otherwise close it with that row open. The assignee and footer notes are the seat's and touch no contract. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` was not measured locally; `Build Core` is green on this head.

- **The dev's two out-of-scope notes.** The `ctx.selection.ids` hole exists in `ActionRunner.ts` and the spec's `target` description does not list it; not teaching it is right. The `record.id` hole in `content/docs/ui/create-vs-edit-form.mdx` is a page button's params, a different surface. Neither is reviewed here.
- **An example app still carries the old shape.** `examples/app-todo`: `todo_mass_complete` sits on `list_toolbar` and its handler reads the old key. By the readings in ① a toolbar click hands that handler no ids. It is outside this diff and outside the skills package, so it is the seat's follow-up, not a change to this PR. A search of open issues found no card for it.
- **Two glosses outside the diff.** The `ACTION_LOCATIONS` comment in `action.zod.ts` and `content/docs/protocol/objectui/actions.mdx` still gloss `list_toolbar` as "(bulk actions, …)". Neither names a key. For the same follow-up.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-ui/rules/actions.md` holds on its main claim.** I tried to break it four ways: a path that delivers the old key (none: the console never sends it, and the server refuses or ignores it); a `list_toolbar` launch that carries an id array (none); an aggregate entry whose named action loses its params or its body's `input` (neither); a `bulkActions` name that runs once for the selection because the action declares `execution: 'aggregate'` (it does not: the promoted def carries no `execution`, the run is per row, and lint refuses the pairing). One clause does not hold as written:

**S2 (should-fix) — "a sent `selectedIds` is refused" is true only beside declared `params`.** `enforceActionParams` in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts` returns before the validator for an action that declares no `params` and is not a declarative update: that action keeps the pass-through. The example declares `params`, so for it the clause is true, and that is the case the PR body measured (the validator, not the dispatcher above it). Many aggregate actions declare none (an export, an archive), and for those a sent `selectedIds` is accepted and the body reads `_selectedIds` as absent. The bullet states the refusal for every aggregate action. Narrow the clause to an action that declares `params`, or drop it; dropping it also pays tokens back to a file with two of headroom.

**`skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json` holds.** Case 3 no longer pins the wrong key or the wrong placement, its tokens are consistent with its own expected answer, and it forbids the old spelling without tripping on the new one.

**N1 (nit) — the `list_toolbar` row says "its body never gets the selection"; with exactly one row ticked the body gets that row as `recordId`.** This is L1's note N2. The row is exact for what the file calls the selection, the id array. The imprecise case steers an author to the list-view wirings, which is the right place, and produces no wrong metadata. If S2 moves this file, fold it in, for example "its body gets no `_selectedIds`". The same phrase is in case 3's `expected_output`.

**N2 (nit) — the opening paragraph names `rowActions` and `bulkActions` as the placements that satisfy `action-no-placement`, not `bulkActionDefs`.** The lint counts all three, and the worked example now relies on the third. A reader who takes the paragraph literally and names the example in `bulkActions` is stopped by `action-dispatch-contract-mismatch`, loudly. Add the key at the next touch that has room.

**N3 (nit) — the example keeps `successMessage`, which nothing shows on its only placement.** Both bulk dispatchers in `ObjectGrid.tsx` mute the runner's toasts, and the bulk dialog's result panel is the report. The key is valid and harmless. Removing it would pay for N1 or N2.

**N4 (nit) — case 3 accepts only the aggregate answer.** A per-row answer (the action named in `bulkActions`, a body that inserts for `ctx.recordId`) is also correct by the bullet and does not meet the tokens. The worked example makes the aggregate answer the likely one. Accepted deviation; the eval seat can loosen it if a round shows the other answer.
